title_en: Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1. This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution to ensure that the People's Courts fairly and promptly adjudicate administrative cases, resolve administrative disputes, protect the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons and other organizations, and supervise the administrative organs' exercise of their powers according to law.

Article 2. If a citizen, legal person or any other organization considers that an administrative act of an administrative organ or its staff has infringed upon his/her/its lawful rights and interests, he/she/it shall have the right to bring a lawsuit in a People's Court in accordance with this Law.
The administrative act mentioned in the preceding paragraph includes an administrative act made by an organization authorized by laws, regulations or rules.

Article 3. The People's Court shall guarantee the right of citizens, legal persons and other organizations to institute proceedings, and shall accept according to law the administrative cases that should be accepted.
No administrative organ or its staff members shall interfere with or obstruct the People's Court from accepting administrative cases.
The person in charge of the administrative organ being sued shall appear in court to respond to the lawsuit. If he/she cannot appear, he/she shall entrust a corresponding staff member of the administrative organ to appear in court.

Article 4. The People's Courts shall, according to law, independently exercise their adjudicative power over administrative cases, and shall not be subject to interference by any administrative organ, social organization, or individual.
The People's Court shall establish an administrative adjudication division to adjudicate administrative cases.
Article 5. In adjudicating administrative cases, the People's Courts shall take facts as the basis and law as the criterion.
Article 6. In adjudicating administrative cases, the People's Courts shall examine the legality of administrative acts.

Article 7. In adjudicating administrative cases, the People's Courts shall, according to law, apply the systems of collegial panel, withdrawal, public trial, and the system of the second instance being final.
Article 8. The parties to an administrative proceeding shall have equal legal status.

Article 9. Citizens of all nationalities shall have the right to use their own native languages and written languages in administrative proceedings.
In an area where a minority nationality lives together in a concentrated community or where multiple nationalities live together, the People's Court shall conduct adjudication and issue legal documents in the languages and written languages commonly used by the local nationality or nationalities.
The People's Court shall provide translation for participants in proceedings who are not familiar with the languages and written languages commonly used by the local nationality or nationalities.
Article 10. The parties shall have the right to debate in an administrative proceeding.
Article 11. The People's Procuratorate shall have the right to exercise legal supervision over administrative proceedings.
Article 14. The Primary People's Court shall have jurisdiction over first-instance administrative cases.
Article 16. The Higher People's Court shall have jurisdiction over major and complex first-instance administrative cases within its jurisdiction.
Article 17. The Supreme People's Court shall have jurisdiction over major and complex first-instance administrative cases throughout the country.

Article 18. An administrative case shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place where the administrative organ that initially made the administrative act is located. A case that has been subject to reconsideration may also be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place where the reconsideration organ is located.
Upon approval by the Supreme People's Court, a Higher People's Court may, based on the actual circumstances of the trial work, designate certain People's Courts to have cross-administrative region jurisdiction over administrative cases.

Article 19. A lawsuit brought against an administrative compulsory measure restricting personal freedom shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place where the defendant is located or the place where the plaintiff is located.
Article 20. An administrative action arising from immovable property shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place where the immovable property is located.

Article 21. Where a case is within the jurisdiction of two or more People's Courts, the plaintiff may choose one of them to file the action. If the plaintiff files the action with two or more People's Courts that have jurisdiction, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court that first dockets the case.

Article 22. If a People's Court finds that a case it has accepted is not within its jurisdiction, it shall transfer the case to the People's Court that has jurisdiction, and the People's Court to which the case is transferred shall accept it. If the People's Court to which the case is transferred considers that the transferred case is not within its jurisdiction in accordance with the provisions, it shall report to the superior People's Court for designation of jurisdiction and shall not transfer it again on its own.

Article 23. If a People's Court with jurisdiction cannot exercise its jurisdiction due to special reasons, the superior People's Court shall designate another People's Court to exercise jurisdiction.
If a dispute over jurisdiction arises between People's Courts, the parties to the dispute shall resolve it through negotiation. If negotiation fails, they shall report to their common superior People's Court for designation of jurisdiction.

Article 24. A superior People's Court shall have the authority to adjudicate administrative cases of first instance that are under the jurisdiction of a subordinate People's Court.
If a subordinate People's Court considers that an administrative case of first instance under its jurisdiction needs to be adjudicated by a superior People's Court or designated to another court, it may report to the superior People's Court for a decision.

Article 25. A counterparty to an administrative act, and any other citizen, legal person or other organization that has an interest in the administrative act, shall have the right to file an action.
If a citizen who has the right to file an action dies, his or her close relatives may file the action.
If a legal person or other organization that has the right to file an action terminates, the legal person or other organization that succeeds to its rights may file the action.
If during the performance of its duties, a People's Procuratorate discovers that an administrative organ with regulatory and supervisory responsibilities in fields such as ecological environment and resource protection, food and drug safety, state-owned property protection, or the transfer of state-owned land use rights has exercised its powers illegally or failed to act, thereby harming the national interest or the public interest, it shall issue a procuratorial recommendation to the administrative organ, urging it to perform its duties according to law. If the administrative organ fails to perform its duties according to law, the People's Procuratorate shall file an action with the People's Court according to law.

Article 26. If a citizen, legal person or other organization directly files an action with a People's Court, the administrative organ that made the administrative act shall be the defendant.
If after reconsideration, the reconsideration organ decides to uphold the original administrative act, the administrative organ that made the original act and the reconsideration organ shall be co-defendants; if the reconsideration organ modifies the original administrative act, the reconsideration organ shall be the defendant.
If the reconsideration organ fails to make a reconsideration decision within the statutory time limit, and the citizen, legal person or other organization brings an action against the original administrative act, the administrative organ that made the original act shall be the defendant; if they bring an action against the reconsideration organ's inaction, the reconsideration organ shall be the defendant.
If two or more administrative organs make the same administrative act, the administrative organs that jointly made the act shall be co-defendants.
If an administrative organ entrusts an organization to make an administrative act, the entrusting administrative organ shall be the defendant.
If an administrative organ is abolished or its functions are changed, the administrative organ that continues to exercise its functions shall be the defendant.

Article 27. Where there are two or more persons on one or both sides of a party, and the administrative case arises from the same administrative act, or arises from similar administrative acts and the People's Court considers that they can be tried jointly and the parties agree, it shall be a joint action.

Article 28. In a joint action where there is a large number of persons on one side, the parties may elect representatives to conduct the action. The litigation acts of the representatives shall have effect on the parties they represent, but if the representatives change or abandon claims or admit the claims of the opposing party, they shall obtain the consent of the represented parties.

Article 29. A citizen, legal person or other organization that has an interest in the administrative act being sued but has not filed an action, or has an interest in the outcome of the case, may apply to participate in the action as a third party, or be notified by the People's Court to participate in the action.
If a People's Court's judgment imposes obligations on a third party or derogates from a third party's rights and interests, the third party shall have the right to file an appeal according to law.

Article 30. If a citizen lacks capacity to conduct litigation, his or her legal representative shall act for him or her in the action. If the legal representatives shirk their responsibilities of representation, the People's Court shall designate one of them to act in the action.

Article 32. A lawyer acting as a litigation agent shall have the right to consult and copy materials related to the case in accordance with regulations, and to investigate and collect evidence related to the case from relevant organizations and citizens. Materials involving state secrets, trade secrets, and personal privacy shall be kept confidential in accordance with legal provisions.
A party and other litigation agents shall have the right to consult and copy the trial materials of the case in accordance with regulations, except for contents involving state secrets, trade secrets, and personal privacy.

Article 34. The defendant shall bear the burden of adducing evidence for the administrative act it has performed, and shall provide the evidence for performing the administrative act and the normative documents on which it is based.
If the defendant fails to provide evidence or, without justifiable reasons, fails to provide evidence within the time limit, it shall be deemed that there is no corresponding evidence, except where the administrative act being sued involves the lawful rights and interests of a third party and the third party provides evidence.
Article 35. During the course of the action, the defendant and its litigation agent shall not collect evidence from the plaintiff, third party, or witnesses on their own.

Article 36. If the defendant has already collected evidence at the time of making the administrative act but cannot provide it due to force majeure or other legitimate reasons, it may, with the permission of the People's Court, provide it after an extended period.
If the plaintiff or third party raises reasons or evidence that were not raised during the administrative processing procedure, the defendant may, with the permission of the People's Court, supplement the evidence.

Article 37. The plaintiff may provide evidence to prove that the administrative act is illegal. If the evidence provided by the plaintiff is not established, the defendant's burden of adducing evidence shall not be exempted.

Article 38. In a case where the defendant is sued for failing to perform its statutory duties, the plaintiff shall provide evidence that it has submitted an application to the defendant, except in any of the following circumstances:
(1) the defendant shall perform its statutory duties proactively in accordance with its functions;
(2) the plaintiff cannot provide evidence due to justifiable reasons.
In a case concerning administrative compensation or damages, the plaintiff shall provide evidence of the damage caused by the administrative act. If the plaintiff cannot adduce evidence due to the defendant's fault, the defendant shall bear the burden of adducing evidence.
Article 39. The People's Court shall have the authority to require the parties to provide or supplement evidence.

Article 40. The People's Court shall have the authority to collect evidence from relevant administrative organs, other organizations, and citizens. However, it shall not collect evidence that was not gathered by the defendant at the time of making the administrative act in order to prove the legality of the administrative act.

Article 42: Where evidence may be destroyed or become difficult to obtain later, a litigation participant may apply to the People's Court for preservation of evidence, and the People's Court may also take preservation measures on its own initiative.

Article 43: Evidence shall be produced in court and shall be cross-examined by the parties. Evidence involving state secrets, trade secrets or personal privacy shall not be produced in an open court session.
The People's Court shall, in accordance with statutory procedures, conduct a comprehensive and objective examination and verification of evidence. Reasons for evidence not admitted shall be stated in the judgment document.
Evidence obtained by illegal means shall not be used as the basis for determining the facts of a case.

Article 44: For an administrative case that falls within the scope of acceptance of the People's Court, a citizen, legal person or any other organization may first apply to the administrative organ for reconsideration; if dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, it may then institute an action with the People's Court; or it may directly institute an action with the People's Court.
Where laws or regulations provide that an application for reconsideration shall first be made to the administrative organ and an action may be instituted with the People's Court only if dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, the relevant provisions of such laws or regulations shall be followed.

Article 45: A citizen, legal person or any other organization that is dissatisfied with a reconsideration decision may institute an action with the People's Court within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the written reconsideration decision. Where the reconsideration organ fails to make a decision within the statutory time limit, the applicant may institute an action with the People's Court within fifteen days from the expiration of the reconsideration period. Unless otherwise provided by law.

Article 46: Where a citizen, legal person or any other organization directly institutes an action with the People's Court, it shall do so within six months from the date on which it knows or should know that the administrative act was taken. Unless otherwise provided by law.
If an action is instituted in respect of real estate after twenty years from the date on which the administrative act was taken, or for other cases after five years from that date, the People's Court shall not accept the case.

Article 47: Where a citizen, legal person or any other organization applies to an administrative organ to perform its statutory duty to protect the person's or organization's personal rights, property rights or other lawful rights and interests, and the administrative organ fails to perform the duty within two months from the date of receipt of the application, the citizen, legal person or organization may institute an action with the People's Court. Where laws or regulations otherwise provide for the time limit for an administrative organ to perform its duty, such provisions shall prevail.
Where a citizen, legal person or any other organization requests an administrative organ to perform its statutory duty to protect its personal rights, property rights or other lawful rights and interests in an emergency, and the administrative organ fails to perform the duty, the institution of an action shall not be subject to the time limit prescribed in the preceding paragraph.

Article 48: Where a citizen, legal person or any other organization delays the time limit for instituting an action due to force majeure or other reasons not attributable to itself, the period of delay shall not be counted in the time limit for instituting an action.
Where a citizen, legal person or any other organization delays the time limit for instituting an action due to other special circumstances other than those specified in the preceding paragraph, it may apply for an extension of the time limit within ten days after the removal of the obstacle; whether to grant the extension shall be decided by the People's Court.

Article 50: A complaint shall be submitted to the People's Court, and copies thereof shall be provided according to the number of defendants.
Where it is genuinely difficult to write a written complaint, an oral complaint may be made, which shall be recorded in the笔录 by the People's Court; the People's Court shall issue a written certificate indicating the date and inform the other party.

Article 51: Where the People's Court receives a complaint and the conditions for instituting an action provided for in this Law are met, it shall register and accept the case.
Where the court cannot immediately determine whether the conditions for instituting an action provided for in this Law are met, it shall receive the complaint, issue a written certificate indicating the date of receipt, and decide within seven days whether to accept the case. If the conditions for instituting an action are not met, the court shall render a ruling not to accept the case. The ruling shall state the reasons for not accepting the case. If the plaintiff is dissatisfied with the ruling, it may appeal.
Where the content of the complaint is incomplete or contains other errors, the court shall provide guidance and clarification and inform the party at one time of the content to be corrected. The court shall not refuse to accept the complaint on the ground that the conditions for instituting an action are not met without providing guidance and clarification.
Where the court refuses to accept the complaint, fails to issue a written certificate after receiving the complaint, or fails to inform the party at one time of the content of the complaint that needs to be corrected, the party may complain to the higher People's Court, which shall order the court to make corrections and shall impose sanctions according to law on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons.

Article 52: Where the People's Court neither accepts the case nor renders a ruling not to accept the case, the party may institute an action with the court at the next higher level. If the higher People's Court considers that the conditions for instituting an action are met, it shall accept and try the case, or may designate another lower People's Court to accept and try the case.

Article 53: Where a citizen, legal person or any other organization believes that the regulatory documents formulated by a department of the State Council, a local people's government or a department thereof, which serve as the basis for an administrative act, are illegal, it may, when filing an action against the administrative act, concurrently request a review of such regulatory documents.
The regulatory documents prescribed in the preceding paragraph do not include rules (规章).

Article 54: People's Courts shall hear administrative cases in public, except where State secrets, personal privacy are involved, or where otherwise provided by law.
For cases involving trade secrets, if a party applies for a closed hearing, the case may be heard in private.

Article 55: Where a party considers that a judicial officer has an interest in the case or has any other relationship that may affect an impartial adjudication, the party shall have the right to apply for the withdrawal of such judicial officer.
Where a judicial officer considers that he or she has an interest in the case or has any other relationship, the judicial officer shall apply for withdrawal.
The provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall apply to court clerks, interpreters, expert witnesses, and inspection personnel.
The withdrawal of the president of the court acting as the presiding judge shall be decided by the judicial committee; the withdrawal of a judicial officer shall be decided by the president of the court; the withdrawal of other personnel shall be decided by the presiding judge. If a party is not satisfied with the decision, the party may apply for one reconsideration.

Article 57: In a case where a party files a lawsuit against an administrative organ for failure to pay pension, minimum subsistence allowance, or work-related injury or medical social insurance premiums according to law, if the rights and obligations are clear and failure to grant advance execution will seriously affect the plaintiff's life, the People's Court may, upon the plaintiff's application, make an adjudication on advance execution.
If a party is not satisfied with an adjudication on advance execution, the party may apply for one reconsideration. During the reconsideration period, enforcement of the adjudication shall not be suspended.

Article 58: Where the plaintiff, after being summoned by a People's Court by summons, refuses to appear in court without justified reasons, or leaves the courtroom without permission of the court during the hearing, the case may be treated as a withdrawal of the complaint; where the defendant refuses to appear in court without justified reasons, or leaves the courtroom without permission of the court during the hearing, a default judgment may be made.

Article 60: In adjudicating administrative cases, the People's Courts shall not apply mediation. However, cases involving administrative compensation, administrative damages, or those where administrative organs exercise discretion prescribed by laws or regulations may be mediated.
Mediation shall follow the principles of voluntariness and legality, and shall not harm national interests, public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of others.

Article 61: In an administrative action involving an administrative license, registration, levy, expropriation, or an administrative adjudication on a civil dispute, if a party applies for a combined resolution of the related civil dispute, the People's Court may hear them together.
In an administrative action, if the People's Court considers that the adjudication of the administrative case needs to rely on a judgment in a civil action, it may make an adjudication to suspend the administrative action.

Article 62: Before a People's Court pronounces a judgment or an adjudication on an administrative case, if the plaintiff applies to withdraw the complaint, or if the defendant modifies the administrative act it performed, and the plaintiff agrees and applies to withdraw the complaint, whether to permit such withdrawal shall be decided by the People's Court by adjudication.

Article 63: People's Courts shall, in adjudicating administrative cases, take laws, administrative regulations, and local regulations as the basis. Local regulations shall apply to administrative cases occurring within the corresponding administrative region.
People's Courts shall, in adjudicating administrative cases in ethnic autonomous areas, also take the regulations on autonomy and separate regulations of such ethnic autonomous areas as the basis.
People's Courts shall, in adjudicating administrative cases, refer to rules.

Article 64: Where, in the course of adjudicating an administrative case, a People's Court, after review, considers that a regulatory document as prescribed in Article 53 of this Law is illegal, such document shall not be taken as the basis for finding the administrative act lawful, and the People's Court shall make a recommendation for handling the matter to the authority that formulated the document.

Article 65: People's Courts shall make public written judgments and written adjudications that have become legally effective for public inspection, except for content involving State secrets, trade secrets, or personal privacy.

Article 66: Where, in the course of adjudicating an administrative case, a People's Court considers that the person in charge or the person directly responsible of an administrative organ has violated laws or discipline, it shall transfer the relevant materials to the supervisory authority, the administrative organ concerned, or its administrative organ at the next higher level; where it considers that a crime has been committed, it shall transfer the relevant materials to the public security or procuratorial organs.
If the defendant, after being summoned by summons, refuses to appear in court without justified reasons, or leaves the courtroom without permission of the court during the hearing, the People's Court may make a public announcement of the defendant's refusal to appear or early departure, and may make a judicial recommendation to the supervisory authority or the administrative organ at the next higher level of the defendant to impose sanctions on its principal responsible person or the person directly responsible according to law.

Article 67: The People's Court shall, within five days from the date of filing the case, serve a copy of the complaint on the defendant. The defendant shall, within fifteen days from the date of receiving the copy of the complaint, submit to the People's Court the evidence of the administrative act performed and the regulatory documents relied upon, and submit a statement of defense. The People's Court shall, within five days from the date of receiving the statement of defense, serve a copy of the statement of defense on the plaintiff.
The defendant's failure to submit a statement of defense shall not affect the adjudication by the People's Court.

Article 68: In adjudicating administrative cases, People's Courts shall form a collegial panel composed of judges, or composed of judges and people's assessors. The number of members of a collegial panel shall be an odd number of three or more.

Article 69: Where the evidence for an administrative act is conclusive, the application of laws and regulations is correct, and the legal procedures are complied with, or where the grounds for the plaintiff's claim that the defendant should perform a statutory duty or an obligation to make a payment are not established, the People's Court shall render a judgment to reject the plaintiff's claim.

Article 71: Where the People's Court renders a judgment ordering the defendant to perform a new administrative act, the defendant shall not, on the basis of the same facts and reasons, perform an administrative act that is essentially the same as the original administrative act.

Article 72: Where, after trial, the People's Court finds that the defendant fails to perform a statutory duty, it shall render a judgment ordering the defendant to perform such duty within a specified period.

Article 73: Where, after trial, the People's Court finds that the defendant is obligated under law to make a payment, it shall render a judgment ordering the defendant to perform the obligation to make such payment.

Article 75 Where an administrative act has major and obvious illegal circumstances such as the implementing entity lacking the qualification of an administrative subject or having no basis, and the plaintiff applies for confirmation of the nullity of the administrative act, the People's Court shall render a judgment confirming the nullity.

Article 76 Where the People's Court renders a judgment confirming the illegality or nullity, it may at the same time render a judgment ordering the defendant to take remedial measures; if losses are caused to the plaintiff, the defendant shall be ordered to bear compensation liability according to law.

Article 77 Where an administrative penalty is obviously improper, or other administrative acts involve definite errors in the determination or recognition of the amount of money, the People's Court may render a judgment of modification.
Where the People's Court renders a judgment of modification, it shall not increase the obligations of the plaintiff or diminish the rights and interests of the plaintiff, except where an interested party is also a plaintiff and the claims are opposite.

Article 78 Where the defendant fails to perform according to law, fails to perform in accordance with the agreement, or illegally modifies or rescinds an agreement as specified in Item 11 of Paragraph 1 of Article 12 of this Law, the People's Court shall render a judgment that the defendant shall bear liability for continued performance, adoption of remedial measures, or compensation for losses.
Where the defendant modifies or rescinds the agreement specified in Item 11 of Paragraph 1 of Article 12 of this Law lawfully but fails to provide compensation according to law, the People's Court shall render a judgment for compensation.

Article 79 In a case where the reconsideration organ and the administrative organ that made the original administrative act are co-defendants, the People's Court shall render a ruling on the reconsideration decision and the original administrative act together.

Article 80 The People's Court shall publicly pronounce judgments in all cases, whether heard in public or in camera.
Where a judgment is pronounced in court, the written judgment shall be served within ten days; where a judgment is pronounced on a fixed date, the written judgment shall be issued immediately after the pronouncement.
When pronouncing a judgment, the court must inform the parties of their right to appeal, the time limit for appeal, and the People's Court to which the appeal may be made.

Article 81 The People's Court shall render a first-instance judgment within six months from the date of docketing. If an extension is necessary due to special circumstances, it shall be approved by the Higher People's Court; if an extension is necessary for a first-instance case heard by the Higher People's Court, it shall be approved by the Supreme People's Court.
Article 83 An administrative case tried under summary procedure shall be heard by a single judge alone and shall be concluded within forty-five days from the date of docketing.
Article 84 If, during the trial, the People's Court finds that a case is not suitable for summary procedure, it shall rule to convert the case to ordinary procedure.

Article 85 If a party refuses to accept a first-instance judgment of the People's Court, it shall have the right to file an appeal with the People's Court at the next higher level within fifteen days from the date of service of the written judgment. If a party refuses to accept a first-instance ruling of the People's Court, it shall have the right to file an appeal with the People's Court at the next higher level within ten days from the date of service of the written ruling. If no appeal is filed within the time limit, the first-instance judgment or ruling of the People's Court shall become legally effective.

Article 86 For an appeal case, the People's Court shall form a collegial panel and hold a hearing. After reviewing the case files, conducting investigations, and questioning the parties, if the collegial panel finds that no new facts, evidence, or reasons have been presented and a hearing is not necessary, it may also proceed without a hearing.
Article 87 When hearing an appeal case, the People's Court shall conduct a comprehensive review of the judgment or ruling of the original trial People's Court and the alleged administrative act.

Article 88 When hearing an appeal case, the People's Court shall render a final judgment within three months from the date of receipt of the appellate petition. If an extension is necessary due to special circumstances, it shall be approved by the Higher People's Court; if an extension is necessary for an appeal case heard by the Higher People's Court, it shall be approved by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 90 If a party considers that a legally effective judgment or ruling is definitely erroneous, it may apply to the People's Court at the next higher level for a retrial, but the enforcement of the judgment or ruling shall not be suspended.

Article 92 If the president of a People's Court at any level finds that a legally effective judgment or ruling made by that court falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 91 of this Law, or finds that a mediation violates the principle of voluntariness or the content of the mediation agreement is illegal, and considers that a retrial is necessary, the matter shall be submitted to the adjudication committee for discussion and decision.
If the Supreme People's Court finds that a legally effective judgment or ruling of a local People's Court at any level, or a People's Court at a higher level finds that a legally effective judgment or ruling of a People's Court at a lower level, falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 91 of this Law, or finds that a mediation violates the principle of voluntariness or the content of the mediation agreement is illegal, it shall have the authority to bring the case up for trial or to order the lower People's Court to conduct a retrial.

Article 93 If the Supreme People's Procuratorate finds that a legally effective judgment or ruling of a People's Court at any level, or a People's Procuratorate at a higher level finds that a legally effective judgment or ruling of a People's Court at a lower level, falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 91 of this Law, or finds that a mediation agreement harms national interests or public interests, it shall lodge a protest.
If a local People's Procuratorate at any level finds that a legally effective judgment or ruling of a People's Court at the same level falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 91 of this Law, or finds that a mediation agreement harms national interests or public interests, it may submit a procuratorial recommendation to the People's Court at the same level and file it with the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level for record; it may also request the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level to lodge a protest with the People's Court at the same level.
People's Procuratorates at all levels shall have the authority to submit procuratorial recommendations to the People's Court at the same level regarding illegal acts of trial personnel in trial procedures other than the trial supervision procedure.
Article 94: The parties must perform the judgments, rulings and mediation documents of the People's Court that have taken legal effect.

Article 95: Where a citizen, legal person or any other organization refuses to perform a judgment, ruling or mediation document, the administrative organ or the third party may apply to the first-instance People's Court for compulsory enforcement, or the administrative organ may enforce it according to law.

Article 97: Where a citizen, legal person or any other organization neither institutes an action against an administrative act within the statutory time limit nor performs it, the administrative organ may apply to the People's Court for compulsory enforcement, or enforce it according to law.
Article 98: This Law shall apply to administrative actions instituted by foreigners, stateless persons or foreign organizations in the People's Republic of China. Unless otherwise provided by law.

Article 99: Foreigners, stateless persons and foreign organizations that institute administrative actions in the People's Republic of China shall have the same litigation rights and obligations as citizens and organizations of the People's Republic of China.
Where a foreign court imposes restrictions on the administrative litigation rights of citizens and organizations of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall apply the principle of reciprocity to the administrative litigation rights of citizens and organizations of that country.

Article 100: Where foreigners, stateless persons or foreign organizations that institute administrative actions in the People's Republic of China entrust lawyers to act as litigation agents, they shall entrust lawyers from a law firm in the People's Republic of China.

Article 101 In the trial of administrative cases by the People's Court, regarding time periods, service, property preservation, court hearing, mediation, suspension of action, termination of action, summary procedure, enforcement, etc., and the supervision by the People's Procuratorate over the acceptance, trial, adjudication, and enforcement of administrative cases, where this Law has no provisions, the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China shall apply.

Article 102 The People's Court shall collect litigation costs when trying administrative cases. The litigation costs shall be borne by the losing party, and if both parties are at fault, they shall be shared by both parties. The specific measures for collecting litigation costs shall be separately prescribed.
Article 103 This Law shall come into force as of October 1, 1990.
